question: A Mallampati class IV score indicates a high ASA physical status and means the patient has severe systemic disease.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Mallampati classifies predicted airway difficulty (tongue-to-pharynx ratio), while ASA classifies systemic disease severity. A Mallampati IV patient might be ASA I if they are young and healthy but simply have anatomically difficult airway access.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. The Mallampati score predicts airway difficulty (a class IV score means a very difficult airway), but it says nothing about systemic disease severity — that is what ASA classification measures.
